observer: Claude (Opus 5.5), 9 Nov 2026: the raw scan (1955 x 1393) blurred 3x3, overview and tiles with a 0.02 grid
covers: one panel seen almost square-on: a pressed sheet with a three-by-three grid of bays and four chamfered corners
notes: VEHICLE: the catalogue gives no vehicle note for this photo; it shares page 92 with the hangar session's g092-a and g092-c, and its paint matches that session, nothing suggests otherwise. WHAT IT IS: neither a lining nor a bench panel. It is rigid pressed sheet steel painted the interior's light grey-green: stiffening ribs in a grid, flat bays, chamfered corners, scratches, a small drilled hole. There is no cloth, no padding and no stitching, and the bench is a separate padded cushion (g092-c). It is the rigid structural panel already registered as hatch.low_profile_panel; the earlier observation (tools/traces/osa_interior/observations/g092-b.json) records the book's text calling it the removable panel for lowering the vehicle. Where it sits is not shown: nothing in the frame locates it (book page 92 prints it beside the right-side racks with no caption of its own). Possible link, not proved: g092-a's top right shows a pressed, mitred-cornered rectangular step in the ceiling at about x 0.6-1.0, y 0-0.13, which may be this kind of panel fitted. Relief: the ribs read as raised bands between flat bays but flash from near the lens gives no firm shadow cue, so whether the ribs stand proud or the bays are sunk is not resolved.
